rationale: This sample is a tiny (5 functions, ~1.2 KB text) floating-point-heavy benchmark whose hot code is the mandel inner loop, so the table favors control-flow obfuscation with modest cost signals: BCF and FLA get the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain since flattening and bogus predicates obscure the loop-structured control flow that a reverse engineer would anchor on, while their elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights let feature matching suppress them in the most iteration-dense blocks; SPLIT is kept cheap and low-risk as a force multiplier that feeds FLA more blocks to flatten; SUB stays lightweight because arithmetic substitution on FP-dominated code adds little semantic hiding but cheap diversity; IBR is included with a high RuntimeCost weight so indirect branching only lands on cold blocks given how punishing indirect jumps are in a tight numeric loop; ICALL and IGV are omitted entirely because with only five functions, one 33-byte emit helper, and virtually no call or global-variable surface, they would pay overhead for near-zero security gain, and the low CorrectnessRisk weights across the board reflect that the simple straight-line/loop structure of this benchmark tolerates transformation well.
